rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-istikhlaṣ means making Yusuf exclusively chosen and specially attached to the king.
rows.anchor: أستخلصه ( أجعله خالصا ( لنفسي ( وخاصا بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause omits Yusuf's arrival for brevity, conveying instant compliance; he was not already with the women, contrary to a reported claim.
rows.anchor: في الكلام إيجاز أي فأتوا به فلما الخ وحذف ذلك للايذان بسرعة الاتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concealed subject of ‘he spoke to him’ is Yusuf and the object is the king; al-Baḥr offers the reverse parsing.
rows.anchor: والضمير المستكن في ( كلمه ) ليوسف عليه السلام والبارز للملك

rows.speaker: أبو حيان في البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr instead takes the king as the first pronoun's subject and Yusuf as its object.
rows.anchor: استظهر في البحر كون الضمير الأول للملك والثاني ليوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king tested Yusuf's speech and found his eloquence confirmed what he had heard about him.
rows.anchor: فاستنطقه ورأى حسن منطقه بما صدق الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makīn means high rank; amīn means trusted with everything, while another gloss is safe from every harm, with trust the fuller honorific.
rows.anchor: مؤتمن على كل شيء وقيل : آمن من كل مكروه والوصف بالامانة هو الابلغ في الاكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Today’ marks the beginning of the status, not its measure; ‘with us,’ the nominal sentence, and its emphasis honor Yusuf.
rows.anchor: ( اليوم ) ليس بمعيار للمكانة والأمانة بل هو آن التكلم والمراد تحديد مبدئهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the messenger ordered Yusuf to leave prison clothes, wash, and dress; Yusuf prayed for prisoners and wrote a maxim on the door before approaching the king in prayer.
rows.anchor: روى أن الرسول جاءه فقال له : أجب الملك الآن بلا معاودة وألق عنك ثياب السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report continues that Yusuf answered the king in seventy languages, recited the dream exactly, and received authority; another version seats him before the interpretation.
rows.anchor: وكان الملك يعرف سبعين لسانا فكلمه بها فأجابه بجميعها فتعجب منه

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq transmits a story that Qifṭīr died and the king married Yusuf to Rāʿīl; she explains her seduction, is reportedly found a virgin, and bears two sons.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن إسحاق قال : ذكروا أن قطفير هلك

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī transmits from Wahb that al-ʿAzīz's needy former wife visits Yusuf, praises obedience that makes slaves kings, receives her needs, and marries him as a virgin.
rows.anchor: أخرج الحكيم الترمذي عن وهب قال : أصابت امرأة العزيز حاجة فقيل لها : لو أتيت يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another version says she met Yusuf on the road, he recognized and married her, and found her a virgin because her former husband was impotent.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أنها تعرضت له في الطريق فقالت ما قالت فعرفها فتزوجها فوجدها بكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The popular storytellers' claim that Yusuf restored her youth and virginity after she had aged is baseless.
rows.anchor: كانت ثيبا غير شابة وهذا مما لاأصل له وخبر تزوجها أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadith scholars do not rely on the marriage report; even if true, its apparent timing is after Yusuf was assigned the storehouses.
rows.anchor: وخبر تزوجها أيضا مما لايعول عليه عند المحدثين وعلى فرض ثبوت التزويج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The storehouses may mean Egypt, the king's territory, or land generally and its produce; Yusuf asks to manage its revenues and distribution.
rows.anchor: أي أرض مصر وفي معناه قول بعضهم أي أرضك التي تحت تصرفك وقيل : أراد بالأرض الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥafīẓ means guarding the stores from the undeserving; ʿalīm means knowing their administration, or famine timing, accounts, and languages.
rows.anchor: بوجوه التصرف فيها وقيل : بوقت الجوع وقيل : حفيظ للحساب عليم بالألسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse permits truthful self-praise when qualifications are unknown and seeking office when able to administer justice and sacred law, even under an unjust or unbelieving ruler; it may be obligatory if a duty depends on this qualified person's appointment.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على جواز مدح الانسان نفسه بالحق إذا جهل أمره : وجواز طلب الولاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophetic warning against asking for authority applies outside the justified cases described here.
rows.anchor: وما في الصحيحين من حديث عبدالرحمن بن سمرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ياعبد الرحمن لا تسأل الأمارة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the king accepted Islam through Yusuf; Yusuf chose this office to manage the famine, the most urgent royal task, rather than merely for general benefit.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد أنه أسلم على يده عليه السلام ولعل إيثاره عليه السلام لتلك الولاية خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Yusuf advised abundant planting in fertile years and storing grain in its stalks, which preserves it and supplies fodder; the king asked him to oversee the plan.
rows.anchor: تزرع في سني الخصب زرعا كثيرا فانك لو زرعت فيها على حجر نبت وتبني الخزائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative leaves the king's acceptance unstated because it was obvious and the broad grant of authority already included the appointment.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه أجابه لذلك حين سأله وإنما لم يذكر إجابته له عليه السلام إيذانا بأن ذلك أمر لامرد له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās a Prophetic saying asking mercy for Yusuf: had he not requested the stores, the king would have appointed him immediately, but delayed a year.
rows.anchor: يرحم الله تعالى أخي يوسف لو لم يقل : ( اجعلني على خزائن الأرض ) لاستعمله من ساعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes Yusuf's investiture with a signet, sword, gemmed golden throne, and robe; he declines the crown as unlike his prophetic forebears, then receives royal authority and establishes justice.
rows.anchor: توجه وختمه بخاتمه ورداه بسيفه ووضع له سريرا من ذهب مكللا بالدر والياقوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During famine Yusuf sold grain successively for money, jewelry, livestock, servants, land, children, and finally the people themselves, lawful in their law; he later freed them and restored their property.
rows.anchor: باع من أهل مصر في سني القحط الطعام في السنة الأولى بالدراهم والدنانير حتى لم يبق منها شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report explains that Yusuf gathered wealth to display God's power and generosity and secure the people's willing obedience and faith, so returning it was not pointless.
rows.anchor: ولعل الحكمة في ذلك اظهار قدرته وكرمه وانقيادهم بعد ذلك لأمره حتى يخلص ايمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf reportedly remained hungry because he feared that eating his fill would make him forget the hungry; he ordered a midday meal to taste hunger, explaining the kings' midday dining custom.
rows.anchor: في تلك المدة فيما يروى لايشبع من الطعام فقيل له : أتجوع وخزائن الأرض بيدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Likewise’ points to wondrous empowerment: God established Yusuf in Egypt, reportedly forty farsakhs square; divine attribution honors him and suggests his authority began from the outset.
rows.anchor: ( وكذلك ( أي مثل التمكين البديع ( مكنا ليوسف ( أي جعلنا له مكانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report gives Egypt's dimensions at forty farsakhs by forty.
rows.anchor: روى أنها كانت أربعين فرسخا في أربعين

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows the lām in ‘for Yusuf’ to be extra; another analysis supplies an omitted object such as the affairs.
rows.anchor: واللام في ( ليوسف ) على ما زعم أبو البقاء يجوز أن تكون زائدة أي مكنا يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatabawwaʾ means settling in the regions; ‘wherever he wills’ may be an adverb or object, as in the verse about where God places His message.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون مفعولا به كما في قوله تعالى : ( الله أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attachment of ‘from it’ to ‘where’ is disputed; the circumstantial parsing is objected to because حيث needs a complement and a circumstantial phrase cannot precede it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بمحذوف وقع حالا من حيث وتعقب بأن ( حيث ) لايتم الا بالمضاف اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is circumstantial of Yusuf; the subject of ‘wills’ may be Yusuf or God by rhetorical shift, supported by readings with the first-person plural.
rows.anchor: والجملة في موضع الحال من يوسف وضمير ( يشاء ) له وجوز أن يكون لله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن كثير والحسن وأبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar, Shaybah, and Nāfiʿ are reported to read ‘We will,’ making God the subject unambiguously.
rows.anchor: أنه قرأ ابن كثير والحسن وبخلاف عنهم أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع ( نشاء ) بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy means worldly favor such as kingship and wealth; interpreting it as prophethood is unsound, and recipients are chosen according to wisdom.
rows.anchor: بنعمتنا وعطائنا في الدنيا من الملك والغنى وغيرهما من النعم وقيل : المراد بالرحمة النبوة وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doers' reward is fulfilled in this world; some identify their good action as faith and steadfast piety, as the following verse indicates.
rows.anchor: والمراد به على ما قيل : الايمان والثبات على التقوى فان قوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative ‘those who believed’ stands for the pronoun ‘doers’; the past and future forms signal persistence, and the possessive marks association with the reward.
rows.anchor: قد وضع فيه الموصول موضع ضمير ( المحسنين ) وجمع بين صيغتي الماضي والمستقبل تنبيها على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative clause after the positive one links divine favor with good action; the emphatic third clause prevents limiting its fruits to immediate reward.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر الجملة الثالثة المؤكدة بعد دفع توهم انحصار ثمرات الاحسان فيما ذكر من الاجر العاجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading restricts mercy to believers persisting in piety; the author says this conflicts with the apparent breadth of ‘whomever We will.’
rows.anchor: ويفهم من ذلك أن المراد ممن نشاء من نشاء أن نصيبه بالرحمة من عبادنا الذين آمنوا واستمروا على التقوى وتعقب بأنه خلاف الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broader reading treats mercy as unearned favor granted as God wills, while reward is earned; believers receive their due in both worlds, and the afterlife reward is greater and lasting.
rows.anchor: ولعل الظاهر حمل ( من ) على ماهو أعم مما ذكروا حينئذ لايبعد أن يراد بالرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says worldly wealth for unbelievers cannot be called mercy; replies cite mercy to believers and unbelievers in this world and the Messenger as mercy to all worlds.
rows.anchor: ظاهر في صحة إطلاق الرحمة على ما يصيب الكافر من ذلك وكذا قوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that God gives no blessing to an unbeliever is attributed to some who define blessing by its good outcome; alternatively mercy may be named with believers in the general group in view.
rows.anchor: وقولهم : ليس لله تعالى نعمة على كافر إنما قاله البعض بناءا على أخذ يحمد عاقبتها في تعريفها

rows.speaker: سفيان ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah says believers are rewarded in both worlds while wrongdoers receive good in this world and no share in the next; his recitation appears to treat worldly benefits as earned.
rows.anchor: نعم يرد على تفسير الرحمة هنا بالنعمة التي لاتكون في مقابلة شيء من الاعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reply allows ‘doers’ to include unbelievers who perform good deeds such as kinship, defending the oppressed, and feeding the poor; nevertheless, Sufyān's report troubles the narrower reading.
rows.anchor: قد يجاب بأنه لعله حمل ( المحسنين ) على ما يشمل الكفار الفاعلين لما يحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some extend ‘we grant’ and ‘we do not waste’ to both worlds, citing no reason for restriction and Sufyān's report; others say restriction gives the next verse a new point and that report derives from the whole passage.
rows.anchor: وعمم بعضهم الأوقات في ( نصيب ولا نضيع ) فقال نصيب في الدنيا والآخرة ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly glosses ‘the doers’ as the patient; if sound, the author considers it especially fitting to the context.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس تفسير ( المحسنين ) بالصابرين ولعله رضي الله تعالى عنه على تقدير صحة الرواية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever interpretation is adopted, Yusuf's promised afterlife reward exceeds his worldly kingship.
rows.anchor: في الآية إشارة أن ما أعد الله تعالى ليوسف عليه السلام من الأجر والثواب في الآخرة أفضل مما أعطاه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's brothers came to buy food after famine reached Canaan and Syria; Jacob sent all but Benjamin to Egypt on reports of a righteous king selling provisions.
rows.anchor: ممتارين لما أصاب أرض كنعان وبلاد الشام ما أصاب مصر وقد كان حل بآل يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf recognized them through keen understanding: their appearance had changed little since their separation as adults, their dress resembled their former dress, and he expected them after the dream's interpretation.
rows.anchor: لقوة فهمه وعدم مباينة أحوالهم السابقة أحوالهم يوم المفارقة لمفارقته إياهم وهم رجال

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Yusuf did not recognize them until they identified themselves; the author objects that the fāʾ after their entry indicates immediate recognition.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال الحسن : ما عرفهم حتى تعرفوا اليه وتعقب ذلك في الانتصاف بأن توسيط الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They failed to recognize Yusuf because of the long interval, his changed state and rank, their changed appearance, and their belief that he had died.
rows.anchor: أي والحال أنهم منكرون له لنسيانهم له بطول العهد وتباين ما بين حاليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say Yusuf kept them at a distance and spoke through an intermediary, or that God withheld recognition so his promised disclosure would be miraculous.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنما لم يعرفوه لأنه عليه السلام أوقفهم موقف ذوي الحاجات بعيدا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognition and denial are customary opposites; their continuing failure is expressed by a nominal sentence, unlike Yusuf's recognition of them.
rows.anchor: وقابل المعرفة بالانكار على ما هو الاستعمال الشائع

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines recognition as knowing through reflection on a trace, narrower than knowledge; its root is finding a scent, and its opposite is denial.
rows.anchor: فعن الراغب المعرفة والعرفان معرفة الشيء بتفكر في اثره فهو أخص من العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf provisioned them and loaded their mounts; reportedly he limited each buyer to one camel-load to ration food fairly, supported by their later request for another load.
rows.anchor: أصلحهم بعدتهم وأوقر ركابئهم بما جاؤا لأجله ولعله عليه السلام إنما باع كل واحد منهم حمل بعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jihāz is what a traveler needs in provisions and goods, and by extension a bride's trousseau or funeral supplies; the reading with kasra on jīm is reported.
rows.anchor: وأصل الجهاز ما يحتاج اليه المسافر من زاد ومتاع وجهاز العروس ماتزف به إلى زوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf says ‘a brother of yours from your father’ rather than ‘your brother’ to feign ignorance, since the possessive form would imply prior knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل بأخيكم مبالغة في اظهار عدم معرفته لهم كأنه لايدري من هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that they asked for Benjamin to receive an extra load; Yusuf granted it while requiring him as a test of their truthfulness.
rows.anchor: ولعله عليه السلام إنما قال ذلك لما قيل : من أنهم سألوه حملا زائدا على المعتاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative account has Yusuf suspect spies, question their family, demand proof, and retain Simeon as hostage; the author objects to the report's timing, accusation against the brothers, and account of the hostage.
rows.anchor: فقال : لعلكم جئتم عيونا تنظرون عورة بلادي قالوا : معاذ الله نحن أخوة بنو أب واحد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Yusuf tapped the king's cup, which disclosed the brothers' betrayal of Joseph, the well, and the false blood on his shirt; the author notes conflicting reports and advises limiting the account to the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وغيره عن ابن عباس أنهم لما دخلوا عليه عليه السلام فعرفهم وهم له منكرون جاء بصواع الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense in ‘I fulfill the measure’ shows that full measure is Yusuf's established practice, although he has just provisioned them.
rows.anchor: أتمه لكم وايثار صيغة الاستقبال مع كون هذا الكلام بعد التجهيز للدلالة على أن ذلك عادة مستمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘I am the best host’ is a circumstantial statement of consistent generosity; the visible measure applies to the current act, while hospitality was already continuous.
rows.anchor: جملة حالية أي ألا ترون أني أوف الكيل لكم ايفاء مستمرا والحال اني في غاية الاحسان في انزالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some generalize both clauses to everyone and take Yusuf's mention of good treatment as encouragement rather than boasting; full measure is a right, hospitality a favor.
rows.anchor: والاقتصار في الكيل على ذكر الايفاء لأن معاملته عليه السلام معهم في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf threatens no measure on their next visit without Benjamin and bars them from entering his land, let alone receiving hospitality.
rows.anchor: إيعاد لهم على عدم الاتيان به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Do not approach me’ may be a prohibition or a negation joined to the consequence; prohibitions may occur as consequences, answering a syntactic objection.
rows.anchor: أي لا تقربوني بدخول بلادي فضلا عن الاحسان في الانزال والضيافة وهو إما نهي أو نفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat shows both sides expected repeated visits; Yusuf's conduct was apparently revealed to him, since kindness would otherwise call for fetching Jacob, but God intended Jacob's trial to be completed.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنهم كانوا على نية الامتياز مرة بعد أخرى وأن ذلك كان معلوما ماله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promise to coax their father gently, while the verb conveys striving and the difficulty of obtaining Benjamin.
rows.anchor: أي سنخادعه ونستميله برفق ونجتهد في ذلك وفي تنبيه على عز المطلب وصعوبة مناله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We will surely do it’ can mean they are able to succeed, or directly promise to fulfill the request without delay.
rows.anchor: أي أنا لقادرون على ذلك لا نتعايا به وانا لفاعلون ذلك لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause reinforces their ability or confirms their promise, without implying that the persuasion happens immediately.
rows.anchor: والجملة على الاول تذييل يؤكد مضمون الجملة الأولى ويحقق حصول الموعود

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatād and others identify the fityān as grain-measuring servants; another view makes them assigned aides.
rows.anchor: لفتيانه ( لغلمانه الكيالين كما قال قتادة وغيره أو لأعوانه الموظفين لخدمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most of the Seven read fityah, a small plural; fityān is preferred because its abundant plural matches the abundant plural of saddle-bags and suits one attendant per bag.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أكثر السبعة ( لفتيه ) وهو جمع قلة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report assigns a man to each saddle-bag to return the payment for food; biḍāʿah is trade capital, and raḥl may mean saddle, mount, or household seat.
rows.anchor: روى أنه عليه السلام وكل بكل رحل رجلا يعني فيه بضاعتهم التي اشتروا بها الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order most naturally follows their provisioning; Yusuf returned the money from generosity and fear Jacob might lack funds, to induce another visit with Benjamin.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا الامر كان بعد تجهيزهم وقيل : قبله ففيه تقديم وتأخير ولا حاجة اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘So they may recognize it’ means recognize the returned payment and its gracious return, or simply identify it after unpacking; the generosity strongly motivates their return.
rows.anchor: أي يعرفون حق ردها والتكرم بذلك فلعل على ظاهرها وفي الكلام مضاف مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Yusuf returned the payment only because nobility forbids charging Jacob conflicts with the stated purpose; support as a duty or preparation for the cup trick is also rejected.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنما فعله عليه السلام لما أنه لم ير من الكرم أن يأخذ من أبيه واخوته ثمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The packed bags clearly present the money as a gift, making an accidental overpayment explanation far-fetched; the brothers later understand it as generosity.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن هيئة التعبية تنادى بأن ذلك بطريق التفضل فاحتمال غيره في غاية البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The measure was denied us’ means they will be denied future grain unless they bring Benjamin, a figurative statement since no denial has yet occurred; it shows repeated visits were expected.
rows.anchor: ( أي حكم بمنعه بعد اليوم أن لم نذهب بأخينا بنيامين حيث قال لنا الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the denial literally: Benjamin was not given a separate camel-load because he was absent.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن الفعل على حقيقته والمراد منع أن يكال لأخيهم الغائب حملا آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naktal means obtaining the needed food; grammarians debate its response syntax and contracted morphology.
rows.anchor: وهو جواب الطلب قيل : والأصل يرفع المانع ونكتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Sijawandī says al-Māzinī corrected Ibn al-Sikkīt's analysis of naktal by asking whether its past would be katal.
rows.anchor: ومن الغريب أنه نقل السجاوندي أنه سأل المازني ابن السكيت عند الواثق عن وزن نكتل

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read yaktal, referring to the brother by proxy because he causes their purchase or his share joins theirs; this supports the literal-denial reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ( يكتل ) بياء الغيبة على اسناده للاخ مجازا لأنه سبب للاكتيال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unvouched report says the brothers greeted Jacob weakly, praised the Egyptian king, and claimed that the king demanded Benjamin and a message about Jacob's grief and illness.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار ولا يخفى حاله أنهم لما دخلوا على أبيهم عليه السلام سلموا عليه سلاما ضعيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's rhetorical question means he cannot entrust Benjamin to them except as he once entrusted Joseph; their betrayal means he cannot rely on them and entrusts the matter to God.
rows.anchor: استفهام إنكاري و ( آمنكم ) بالمد وفتح الميم ورفع النون مضارع من باب علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob hopes God will guard Benjamin and spare him a second calamity; he is leaning toward permission while relying on God.
rows.anchor: فأرجو أن يرحمني بحفظه ولا يجمع علي مصيبتين وهذا كما ترى ميل منه عليه السلام إلى الأذن والارسال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God swore to return the two brothers to Jacob because he relied on Him.
rows.anchor: ولذا روى أن الله تعالى قال : وعزتي وجلالي لأردهما عليك اذ توكلت علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥifẓan is accusative as specification; some parse it circumstantially, which Abū Ḥayyān rejects as wrongly restricting God's superiority, while defenders say the state is constant.
rows.anchor: ونصب ( حافظا ) على التمييز نحو لله دره فارسا وجوز غير واحد أن يكون على الحالية

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects to the circumstantial parsing because it conditions God's superiority; the author notes the reply and further dispute.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه أبو حيان بأنه ليس بجيد لما فيه من تقييد الخيرية بهذه الحالة

rows.speaker: أكثر السبعة
rows.claim: Most of the Seven read ḥifẓan; al-Aʿmash has singular genitive ḥāfiẓ, and Abū Hurayrah plural genitive ḥāfiẓīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أكثر السبعة ( حفظا ) ونصبه على ما قال أبو البقاء على التمييز لاغير

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's transmitted reading adds ‘He is the best of protectors’; Abū Ḥayyān says the phrase is commentary, not Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ونقل ابن عطية عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه قرأ ( فالله خير حافظا وهو خير الحافظين )

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines matāʿ as anything useful; here it can mean food or its container, associated because the food is inside the vessel.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : المتاع كل ماينتفع به على وجه وهو في الآية الطعام وقيل : الوعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They found their payment returned as a favor, which they understood from the circumstances.
rows.anchor: وجدوا بضاعتهم ( التي كانوا أعطوها ثمنا للطعام ( ردت إليهم ( أي تفضلا

rows.speaker: علقمة ويحيى بن وثاب والأعمش
rows.claim: ʿAlqamah, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, and al-Aʿmash read raddat with kasra on rāʾ after transferring the geminated dāl's vowel, a Banū Ḍabbah dialect also found in qīl and bīʿ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علقمة ويحيى بن وثاب والأعمش ( ردت ) بكسر الراء وذلك أنه نقلت حركة الدال المدغمة إلى الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If baghy means seeking, mā may be an interrogative object: what more could they seek after the king's kindness? A report has them tell Jacob no relative could show them greater generosity.
rows.anchor: فما يحتمل أن تكون استفهامية منصوبة المحل على أنها مفعول مقدم لنبغي فالمعنى ماذا نطلب وراء ما وصفنا لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Our payment was returned’ explains the favor's extent; the passive stresses either hidden kindness they did not notice or an obvious praiseworthy agent.
rows.anchor: جملة مستأنفة موضحة لما دل عليه الانكار من بلوغ اللطف غايته كأنهم قالوا : كيف لا وهذه بضاعتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: N-m-r means bringing provisions; they will feed their family, protect Benjamin as promised, and gain another camel-load under the king's rationing practice.
rows.anchor: ونمير أهلنا ( أي نجلب لهم الميرة وهي بكسر الميم وسكون الياء طعام يمتاره الانسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That is a small measure’ may refer to their first allotment, insufficient for the family and thus requiring another visit with Benjamin.
rows.anchor: أي قليل لايقوم بأودنا يحتمل أن يكون اشارة إلى ما كيل لهم أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead refer to the total load their camels can carry, explaining their need for an increase.
rows.anchor: إن ماتحمله أباعرنا قليل لايكفينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the extra camel-load is small or easy for the king, answering the worry that he would consider more than ten loads excessive.
rows.anchor: ذلك الكيل الزائد قليل لايضايقنا فيه الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may refer to the total proposed allotment including Benjamin's load, which they present as easy and without hardship to persuade Jacob.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ذلك إشارة إلى الكيل الذي هم بصدده وتضمنه كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some make ‘that small measure’ Jacob's reply: one camel-load is not worth risking a child for, though it would fit more naturally beside his surrounding speech.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم كون ذلك من كلام يعقوب عليه السلام والاشارة إلى كيل البعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā nabghī may ask what goal they seek, with later clauses explaining their benefits; al-Kashf instead coordinates the whole question with those clauses because all aim to win Jacob's consent.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معنى ( ما نبغي ) أي مطلب نطلب من مهماتنا والجمل الواقعة بعده

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو حيوة
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Abū Ḥayyah read tabghī addressing Jacob: what more is needed beyond their benefits, or what evidence of the king's favor could he want?
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبو حيوة ( ما تبغي ) بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾishah transmits the Prophetic reading addressed to Jacob and its sense as asking what more is wanted after the benefits or king's kindness.
rows.anchor: وروت عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم والخطاب ليعقوب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may be negative with an omitted object: they seek nothing beyond the king's kindness or listed benefits; if baghy means transgression, it denies lying or departing from propriety.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون ( ما ) نافية ومفعول ( نبغي ) محذوف أن ما نبغي شيئا غير ما رأيناه

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī reads their appeal as sound advice to Jacob, with each clause explaining why a kind king makes protection easy.
rows.anchor: وقال العلامة الطيبي : إنما صح التأكيد والتذييل لأن الكلام في الامتياز

rows.speaker: عائشة وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
rows.claim: ʿĀʾishah and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read numīr with ḍamma; the lexicon records mār and amār for supplying one's family.
rows.anchor: وقرأت عائشة وأبو عبدالرحمن السلمي ( ونمير ) بضم النون وقد جاء مار عياله وأمارهم بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob refuses to send Benjamin after prior suffering and requires a binding pledge from God, understood as an oath by God that strengthens the covenant.
rows.anchor: ( بعد أن عاينت منكم ما أجرى المدامع ( حتى تؤتون موثقا من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You will surely bring him’ answers an implicit oath: they must swear to bring Benjamin.
rows.anchor: جواب قسم مضمر إذ المعنى حتى تحلفوا بالله وتقولوا والله لنأتينك به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says Jacob required an oath by Muhammad as final prophet; the author considers it apparently unsound, while al-ʿImādī instead has them swear by God, Lord of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وفي مجمع البيان نقلا عن ابن عباس أنه عليه السلام طلب منهم أن يحلفوا بمحمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم خاتم النبيين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses ‘unless you are surrounded’ as being overwhelmed by enemies or destroyed, deriving the expression from enemy encirclement that commonly ends in death.
rows.anchor: ( أي الا أن تغلبوا فلا تطيقوا ذلك أو الا أن تهلكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be a free exception from all circumstances, but this is challenged because أن plus a verb cannot act as a circumstantial verbal noun; a reply takes ‘circumstance’ in its ordinary sense, though the author finds difficulty with it.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء قيل مفرغ من أعم الأحوال والتقدير لتأتنني به على كل حال إلا حال الإحاطة بكم

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr says Ibn al-Anbārī rejects making the derived verbal noun an adverb of time, whereas Ibn Jinnī permits it, citing Abū Dhuʾayb's line.
rows.anchor: لم يجز عند ابن الأنباري لأنه يمنع وقوع المصدر المؤول ظرفا

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب الهذلي
rows.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb's line about no mother being more distressed when her little one is harmed is cited as evidence for Ibn Jinnī's permissive construction.
rows.anchor: وتالله ماإن شهلة ( 1 ) أم واحد + بأوجد مني أن يهان صغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis treats the exception as a cause under implied negation: they will bring him unless overwhelmed; the free-exception reading also needs generality over every feasible circumstance.
rows.anchor: وقيل : من أعم العلل على تأويل الكلام بالنفي الذي ينساق اليه أي لتأتنني

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abū al-Suʿūd distinguishes mere fulfillment despite no impediment from exceptions that require accompanying every circumstance; a critic raises three objections that the author finds unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: وتعقب المولى أبو السعود تجويز الأول بلا تأويل بقوله : وأنت تدري أنه حيث لم يكن الاتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers gave the covenant; Jacob invokes God as trustee, and the present tense makes the exchange vivid so they remember and honor it; wakīl means watchful guardian and one who requites.
rows.anchor: عرضنا لثقته بالله تعالى وحثا لهم على مراعاة حلفهم به عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wakīl means an overseeing guardian; some explain that God will requite them for the covenant.
rows.anchor: أي مطلع رقيب فان الموكل بالامر يراقبه ويحفظه قيل : والمراد أنه سبحانه مجاز على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob counsels separate gates to guard against the evil eye: the brothers were handsome and conspicuous, and the king's unusual favor could invite envy; they had been unknown on the first trip.
rows.anchor: نهاهم عليه السلام عن ذلك حذرا من اصابة العين فانهم كانوا ذوي جمال وشارة حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another suggestion is that Jacob especially feared for Benjamin, loved as solace for Joseph; the author rejects explanations that the advice was to avoid suspicion as spies or overhear news of Joseph.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون خوفه عليه السلام عليهم من العين في هذه الكرة بسبب أن فيهم محبوبه وهو بنيامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic reports establish that the eye is real, can precede destiny, and should be answered by washing; it can send a person to the grave and a camel to the pot, and the Prophet prayed protection for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn.
rows.anchor: والعين حق كما صح عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وصح أيضا بزيادة ولو كان شيء سابق القدر سبقته العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A philosophical taxonomy distinguishes four directions of effect: psyche on psyche or body, and body on body or psyche.
rows.anchor: وهو أن تأثير شيء في آخر إما نفساني أو جسماني وكل منهما إما في نفساني أو جسماني فالانواع أربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first psyche-to-psyche type includes direct knowledge from higher principles, as with prophetic knowledge received without prior study.
rows.anchor: أما النوع الأول أعني تأثير النفساني في مثله فكتأثير المبادئ العالية في النفوس الانسانية بافاضة العلوم والمعارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imaginative psyche-to-psyche type includes disclosure of past or future matters, dreams, inspirations, and magic that exploits weak imaginative faculties.
rows.anchor: وثانيهما مايتعلق بالتخيل القوي بأن يلقى إلى من يكون مستعدا له ما يقوى به على تخيلات الامور الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psyche affecting body includes control of one's own body, prophetic miracles affecting the world through prayer, and harmful magic that can cause illness or death.
rows.anchor: وأما النوع الثاني أعني ثأثير النفساني في الجسماني فكتأثير النفوس الانسانية في الابدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Body-to-body effects include medicines, poisons, talismans, and natural properties such as a magnet attracting iron, sometimes aided by celestial configurations.
rows.anchor: وأما النوع الثالث وهو تأثير الجسماني في الجسماني فكتأثير الأدوية والسموم في الأبدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Body-to-psyche effects include appealing or repellent images, music, dance, and eloquence, invoking the saying that some eloquence is sorcery.
rows.anchor: وأما النوع الرابع وهو تأثير الجسماني في النفساني فكتأثير الصور المستحسنة أو المستقبحة في النفوس الانسانية

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī emphatically denies the evil eye without offering a proof; most Sunnis, Muʿtazilites, and others affirm it but differ on its mechanism.
rows.anchor: فأبوا على الجبائي أنكرها انكارا بليغا ولم يذكر لذلك شبهة فضلا عن حجة

rows.speaker: الجاحظ
rows.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ says physical particles extend from the eye to the admired person, affecting the body like poison.
rows.anchor: فقال الجاحظ : إنه يمتد من العين أجزاء فتصل بالشخص المستحسن فتؤثر فيه تأثير السم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qāḍī objects that al-Jāḥiẓ's particle theory should make the eye affect an unattractive person as well as an admired one.
rows.anchor: وضعف ذلك القاضي بأنه لو كان الأمر كما قال لوجب أن تؤثر العين في الشخص الذي لا يستحسن

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī replies that admiration creates fear of losing a loved object or grief that an enemy possesses it; both concentrate and heat the spirit, producing a hot eye-ray.
rows.anchor: فانه يحصل عند ذلك الاستحسان خوف شديد من زواله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayrah in Aḥmad's Musnad, with reliable transmitters according to al-Haythamī, says the eye is real and Satan and human envy harm through it, apparently opposing al-Rāzī's account.
rows.anchor: رجاله رجال الصحيح أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : العين حق يضرها الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports prescribe the afflicter washing the face, hands, elbows, knees, feet, and inner garment, then pouring the water over the afflicted person; reports differ on including hips or genitals.
rows.anchor: وكيفية ذلك أن يغسل العائن وجهه ويديه ومرفقيه وركبيته وأطراف رجليه وداخل ازاره

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Some consider washing recommended; al-Māwardī and others require it because of the imperative and its proven healing effect.
rows.anchor: وقال الماوردي تبعا للجماعة : للوجوب فيجب على العائن أن يغسل

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī explains washing as cooling heat; Ibn al-Qayyim compares it to an antidote from a snake and extinguishing a flame from the afflicter's trace, which the author calls fuller despite limitations.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن ذلك أمر تعبدي وهو مخالف لما أشار اليه الامام من كون الحكمة فيه تبريد تلك السخونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The defense of al-Jāḥiẓ fails to explain reports of afflicters harming a person described to them from many farsakhs away, too distant for particles to travel.
rows.anchor: ما ثبت من أن بعض العائنين قد يصيب ما يوصف له ويمثل ولو كان بينه وبينه فراسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Selected Sunni investigators explain the eye as a psyche-to-body effect not limited to heat, cold, moisture, or dryness; fear can cause a fall from a plank when it is high, and mental images change the body.
rows.anchor: وقال الحكماء واختاره بعض المحققين من أهل السنة : إن ذلك من تأثير النفساني بالجسماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because souls differ, some can alter another body when they see or imagine it with admiration; experience confirms this, usually associated with the gaze although the soul is the true cause.
rows.anchor: وأيضا جواهر النفوس مختلفة فلا يمتنع أن يكون بعض النفوس بحيث تؤثر في تغير بدن حيوان آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the true agent by consensus; one account says He creates effects through causes without necessary dependence, while the Ashʿarī account says they occur alongside causes with no causal role.
rows.anchor: والفاعل للآثار في الحقيقة هو الله عز سلطانه بالاجماع لكن جرت عادته تعالى على خلقها بالاسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophetic statement that the eye is real means psychic influence through it is divinely decreed, like familiar effects of fire, water, and medicine; all remains subject to God's will.
rows.anchor: فمعنى قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : العين حق أن اصابة النفس بواسطتها أمر كائن مقضي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wisdom for God's creating the eye's effect is unknown to us.
rows.anchor: وحكمة خلق الله تعالى التأثير في مسئلة العين أمر مجهول لنا

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم وأبو القاسم البلخي
rows.claim: Abū Hāshim and Abū al-Qāsim al-Balkhī explain the eye through moral benefit: God changes an admired object to loosen attachment, but remembrance and prayer can change the benefit so the object remains.
rows.anchor: وزعم أبو هاشم وأبو القاسم البلخي أن ذلك مما يرجع إلى مصلحة التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invocation and appeal to God are valid means of warding off the eye and may return its harm to the afflicter; Ibn ʿAsākir reports a story beginning with advice to guard a camel.
rows.anchor: ثم ان ما أشار اليه من نفع ذكر الله تعالى والالتجاء اليه سبحانه حق فقد صرحوا بأن الادعية والرقي
